title: Unaffordable treatment and limited care support put Roma well-being and household security at risk
source: Source: 2025 Multi-Country Survey on Socio-Economic Vulnerabilities of Roma, surveyed communities in Zakarpattia Oblast. Quotes from the micro-narratives study, collected across several regions of Ukraine.

sections.title: Poor health restricts opportunities during the working years

content.content: Poor health is more common among working-age Roma than among their non-Roma neighbors. For people relying on physically demanding or irregular work, this can affect both their ability to earn and the household’s resources for care.

content.subTitle: Reporting of bad or very bad health within each age group.

microViz.text: Roma aged 25 to 64 report bad or very bad health

sections.title: Insurance does not ensure affordable treatment

content.content: Most Roma have medical insurance, yet treatment remains unaffordable for some. Medicines, tests and travel compete with food, heating and other essentials.

content.title: Medical insurance and unmet care needs
content.subTitle: The insurance measure covers respondents; unmet care covers those who needed treatment in the previous year.

data.label: Did not get care when needed

content.content: Regular medicine costs can leave little for other needs, even before additional treatment becomes necessary:
“...they asked for 15,000 for the operation. I don’t have that money right now. [...] So, all the money I receive goes to medicine. I don’t have enough for food or anything else.”
content.author: Female, aged 65 and over

content.content: Travel adds another cost, particularly in remote settlements. A nearby facility may still be difficult to use without affordable transport or money for treatment.

sections.title: Limited support for care reduces the options for earning a living

content.content: When a child or an older relative needs constant care, someone has to stay home, usually a woman. For Roma women, who already have far fewer openings to pursue paid work than other women, care can clog the remaining ones.
One mother caring for four children, including a son with a disability, described being unable to work:
“No, I can’t. I have four children, and I take care of all of them on my own.”
content.author: Female, aged 30 to 49

content.content: Care holds families together, but it is paid for in earnings the household cannot spare.
